title: Analysis of Electric Field Shielding Characteristics on Residential Platforms and Optimization of Shielding Position Near 1000 kV Double-Circuit Transmission Lines on the Same Tower
abstract: The electric field strength beneath 1000 kV ultra-high-voltage transmission lines is relatively high, posing a risk of excessive electric field exposure in the presence of nearby buildings. Shielding wires are an effective technical measure to mitigate excessive electric field strength at sensitive locations; however, optimal performance depends on the appropriate selection of shielding parameters such as wire size and placement. In this study, a 6 m × 6 m building platform was constructed beneath a 1000 kV double-circuit transmission line mounted on a single tower. Shielding wires with heights of 5 m, 6 m, and 7 m were installed. The electric field distribution above the building, as well as the shielding effects, were analyzed. The optimal positioning of the shielding wires was also investigated. The results indicate that the electric field on the upper surface of the platform closest to the transmission line side can reach 5 kV/m, while the electric field on the second-level platform can reach up to 7.5 kV/m. A single shielding wire can reduce the electric field strength by 21.7%, whereas multiple wires can achieve reductions of more than 30%. We convert the above electric field model into a mathematical model and propose an optimization method for the shielding wires position. When the height of the shielding wire is less than 8 m, the optimal placement is approximately directly above the sensitive point. These findings provide practical guidance for mitigating electric fields near sensitive areas and offer a technical foundation for the design and installation of shielding wires.

title: A Hybrid Multi-Criteria Decision-Making Based Fuzzy System for Comprehensive Health Assessment of Power Transformers
abstract: Precise evaluation of transformer health using well-structured asset management methodologies is essential, and over the last two decades, several health assessment methods have been developed based on various diagnostic tests. However, the literature on methods to ensure a comprehensive health evaluation with a focus on prioritized correlation analysis is limited. In this context, this work proposes a framework for evaluating the performance of power transformers using 15 diagnostic attributes. The model is designed with Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP), Grey Relational Analysis (GRA), and Technique for Order Performance by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). The diagnostic attributes are initially normalized, and then prioritized based on closely related characteristics and finally grouped into three specific health degrees using the proposed systematic hybrid decision-making approach. The three health degrees are further coupled with a technical fuzzy rule base to derive the actual health status of power transformers. The hybrid model is validated using known health conditions of 200 transformers collected from Himachal Pradesh State Electricity Board, India, and compared with recent similar health prediction methods published in the literature. The comparison reveals the superiority of the model with 97% accuracy. Moreover, the following are the main advantages of the model over the existing health assessment methods: prioritization among closely related attributes, assessment of samples with respect to positive and negative ideal solutions, no dependency on training data, less complexity, and consideration of visual inspection and maintenance parameters. Furthermore, it facilitates an appropriate alert system for conditional maintenance.

title: Anisotropic Bulk Conductivity of Epoxy Resin-Impregnated Paper Under Thermal Aging: Effects on Gas-Solid Interface Insulation Performance in HVDC Bushings
abstract: Valve-side bushings for ultra-high voltage (UHV) converter transformers serve as critical components in UHV direct current transmission systems. Epoxy resin-impregnated paper (RIP), employed as the dry-type insulation of bushings, endures prolonged exposure to high-voltage and high-current conditions, leading to significant thermal aging. In this study, valve-side bushings of a ±800 kV converter transformer were investigated through thermal aging experiments conducted on the RIP specimens, which were sectioned from the bushing insulation along the radial and axial directions, respectively. The results showed that the RIP insulation exhibits anisotropic bulk conductivity due to its inherent structural anisotropy. This anisotropy intensified with aging time, with the initial anisotropy ratio of 5 to 25 rising to 6 to 38 after thermal aging at 115°C. The simulation results of the ±800 kV bushing revealed that under anisotropic conditions, substantial negative charges accumulate at the bushing end, thereby enhancing the electric field within the SF6 gas gap. This phenomenon is further intensified after thermal aging, resulting in an average electric field strength of 2.31 kV/mm and giving rise to both significant tangential and normal electric field components. Such field distortion elevates the risk of surface flashover initiated by partial discharges in the gas gap, suggesting progressive insulation degradation over the operational lifespan of the bushings.

title: Active voltage-drop arc suppression and property identification methods for generator stator ground fault
abstract: Single-phase stator winding ground fault is one of the most frequent faults in the marine nuclear power platform. The internal space of the platform is compact and contains the nuclear reactor loads, so it is sensitive to the arcing process and needs reliable arc suppression. Therefore, the active voltage-drop arc suppression and fault property identification methods are presented in this paper. For the fault point location method constructed by the fundamental potentials, multiple solutions may be calculated under certain fault conditions. Thus, a low frequency injection-based checking criterion is proposed to determine the unique location result. On this basis, the arc suppression compensation currents containing the fundamental and third harmonic components can be calculated and injected into the generator neutral point. Since the neutral point voltage is controlled to be equal to the amplitude of the fault potential and the phase is opposite, the fault point voltage is suppressed to zero, and effective arc suppression is realized. The fault property identification is realized by using the value difference of the grounding transition resistance. Thus, transient and permanent fault conditions are distinguished. Simulation and dynamic experiment results verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Coordinated Control and Protection Strategy for Transmission Lines Connected to Grid-Forming Inverter-Based Resources
abstract: Compared to traditional grid-following (GFL) control, grid-forming (GFM) inverters possess the capability to actively support the grid; however, they retain the inherent characteristics of limited fault current amplitude and controlled phase. To address the degraded adaptability of distance protection on outgoing transmission lines integrated with GFM inverters, this paper proposes a coordinated strategy between GFM control and distance protection. First, based on the compound sequence network, the analytical relationship between the additional reactance component and the fault current phase is analyzed. Consequently, ideal fault current phases required to eliminate measurement errors are derived. Second, an adaptive virtual impedance control-protection coordination strategy based on sequence component separation is proposed. The positive-sequence control loop regulates parameters to track the ideal phase and eliminate the measured reactance error, while the negative-sequence loop suppresses voltage unbalance and provides voltage support. PSCAD/EMTDC simulations demonstrate that, without modifying existing protection configurations or requiring remote communication, the proposed strategy effectively eliminates the impact of the additional reactance. Consequently, it ensures the reliable operation of distance protection and maintains excellent adaptability and reliability in multi-IBR scenarios.

title: Structural Design and Performance Optimization of Flexible Connection Structure of On-Load Tap Changer under Transient Electro-Thermo-Mechanical Coupling
abstract: On-load tap changers (OLTCs) rely on flexible connection structures (FCSs) to maintain conductive circuits between moveable contacts. Stress concentration represents a primary cause of FCS mechanical failure, yet its behavior under transient electro-thermo-mechanical coupling conditions remains insufficiently addressed. This study develops a shape optimization method based on parametric curves and adaptive optimization to mitigate stress concentration in FCSs. Transient coupling stress analyses are performed for both fixed and moveable FCS types, and geometry-specific parametric curves are constructed according to the identified stress concentration locations and their underlying causes. Adaptive parameter optimization yields significant stress reductions in both cases. The analysis is further extended to multiple consecutive switching cycles, providing a more realistic assessment of FCS stress evolution under actual OLTC service conditions.

title: A Fault Location Method Based on Electrode-Seawater Loop Characteristic Frequency Band Signal Injection for Undersea Observation Network
abstract: Submarine cable fault location in undersea observation networks presents significant challenges due to limited measurement data and the complex impedance of the seawater loop. The presence of the frequency-dependent effect of seawater-electrode impedance significantly impacts the accuracy of fault distance measurement, similar to the effect of an unknown transition resistance. This paper proposes a new frequency band signal active injection fault location method. The frequency-dependent characteristics of the submarine cable electrode-seawater system were analyzed. The electrochemical processes at the electrode-seawater interface, including Faradaic reactions and double-layer effects, were thoroughly investigated. An electrode-seawater impedance model was developed, incorporating seawater impedance, Faradaic impedance, and double-layer capacitance. Based on this model, a full-loop impedance calculation method suitable for DC power supply systems was proposed. The quantitative relationship between fault distance, transition resistance, and the total transmission circuit impedance was further explored. A fault location function was introduced to quantify the correlation between these variables. Using signal injection technology at the shore station, the method effectively overcomes the challenges of data acquisition under limited measurement points and enables accurate location of submarine cable faults. By considering the impedance characteristics of the electrode across different frequency bands and integrating the characteristic impedance and reflection coefficients of the submarine cable, the signal injection frequency range was optimized, significantly improving fault location accuracy. The location function, which is inherently implicit, is solved using the damped nonlinear least-squares iteration method, ensuring efficient and precise fault distance calculation. Study cases demonstrate that this method achieves high-precision fault location in submarine cables and exhibits robustness for various fault locations and resistances.

title: Dual Grid-Forming MMC With Embedded Storage for Damping Provision
abstract: This paper explores the use of the recently proposed dual grid-forming control applied to modular multilevel converters and enhanced by embedded energy storage. Dual grid-forming technique enables the converter to form both ac and dc grids by leveraging its internal energy, while the embedded energy storage provides damping to the grid, thereby improving its stability margins. The application of dual grid-forming in a modular multilevel converter is characterized by using its internal power balance as a synchronization mechanism. The addition of controllable and decoupled energy storage provides a new and promising degree of freedom. On this basis, two innovative damping provision methods are proposed and compared with the existing solutions by means of small-signal eigenvalue analysis and time-domain numerical simulations. Results show enhanced system stability margins, with an increased damping ratio of the critical eigenvalue from 10% to 60%, and a lower perturbation of system variables when using the proposed strategies.

title: Practical Solutions to Volt-Var Optimization Under Uncertainty via Blackbox Optimization
abstract: In this work, we propose an optimal reactive power dispatch (ORPD) stochastic program for volt-var optimization (VVO) of power distribution networks. The formulation considers not only control settings of conventional VVO devices, e.g., voltage regulators, capacitor banks, and on-load tap changers, but also optimal settings for volt-var droop curves of distributed energy resources (DERs), compliant with the IEEE 1547-2018 standard. Instead of including the power flow equations in the optimization problem which makes it nonlinear and nonconvex, a power flow solver is utilized and the problem is solved by blackbox optimization (BBO). The feasibility of the derived solution is improved by using unbalanced power flow simulations. The solution is effective under various demand and DER generation scenarios such that device settings are not frequently changed, making it practical for in-field implementations. Through numerical simulations on IEEE test feeders, we illustrate the performance of the solutions of our proposed approach on both in-sample and out-of-sample scenarios. We show that our approach outperforms a benchmark reinforcement learning method, and is also scalable to large-scale distribution networks.

title: A New Approach to the Inverse Power Model in Qualification Load Cycle Planning and Life Estimation for HVDC Extruded Cables
abstract: Cigrè Technical Brochure 852:2021 has confirmed the voltages and durations of qualification load cycles for HVDC extruded cables as in former Technical Brochures 219:2003 and 496:2012. These values rely on the Inverse Power Law Model with life exponent set to n = 10, considered in Cigrè 852 a conservative basis for estimating cable life. The value n = 10 has been left unchanged over more than 20 years to date despite new compounds with n up to 26 have emerged thanks to the technological improvement of polymeric DC cable insulation. Relying on this Technical Brochure 852, so far the author has used the same approach to estimate the life of HVDC extruded cables under qualification test load cycle conditions. This paper proposes a new approach to the Inverse Power Model in the selection of voltage levels and durations of qualification load cycles. Such new approach exploits the evidence that qualification tests are passed with broad margin by “good” cable systems, and highlights the improved voltage endurance of new cable insulation compounds with greater n. The satisfactory performance of this approach on both these respects is proven by an illustrative application to life estimation of HVDC cables subject to type test load cycles.

title: Suppression of M3C Circulation and Low-Frequency Transmission System Oscillation based on Dual-Synchronous Coordinate System Circulation Control
abstract: Low-frequency transmission based on a modular multilevel matrix converter (M3C) has gradually become one of the new energy delivery methods because it can reduce transmission frequency and increase transmission capacity. However, there are circulating currents with complex frequency and phase sequence characteristics in the M3C bridge arm, which can seriously affect the performance of the equipment and even cause system oscillation. To address this issue, this paper first establishes a mathematical model of multi-frequency circulation distribution in the M3C and proposes a double synchronous coordinate system circulating current(DSRF-CC) suppression strategy. Secondly, the control loop is mapped to the equivalent circuit of the port and the mechanism of the negative damping that induces system oscillation is revealed. Finally, considering the dual constraints of circulating current (CC) and oscillation suppression, the design region of the circulating current suppression control parameters is quantitatively characterized. The accuracy of the research is verified using MATLAB/Simulink simulations.

title: Transient Synchronization Stability of Grid-Tied Virtual Synchronous Generators Under Multiple Uncertainties: A Practical Stability Framework
abstract: Grid-tied virtual synchronous generators (VSGs) face significant uncertainties arising from encapsulated control parameters, volatile renewable injections, and shifting operating conditions. Conventional deterministic stability analysis fails to ensure conservatism under such perturbations. This paper proposes a practical stability framework that focuses on bounded performance within a prescribed error region rather than strict asymptotic convergence. First, a perturbed system model incorporating parameter errors, power fluctuations, and condition variations is established, which is approximated by a deterministic comparison system. Using the unstable equilibrium point of this comparison system, a closed-form critical energy that provides a provably conservative estimate of the region of attraction is derived. Furthermore, the limit cycle of the comparison system is characterized via the Poincaré-Bendixson theorem. Finally, an analytical method is developed to determine the ultimate bound of the perturbed system, thereby delineating the motion range of VSGs under multiple uncertainties.

title: End-to-End Intelligent Cyber Defense for Grid Edge Devices: Methods and Implementation in Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation Testbed
abstract: This paper proposes and validates the operation of an end-to-end machine learning-based cyber defense framework for grid edge devices (GEDs) in distribution systems. The proposed framework establishes redundant communication paths between the GEDs and the utility control center at different levels of communication. Different control and measurement messages are duplicated and transmitted via these redundant paths. The collected duplicated messages are then aggregated using a novel machine learning-based data combination approach that is able to reduce or remove the effect of false data injection attacks (FDIA) on the communication network. The proposed framework defends against FDIA on the data transferring between the GEDs and the control center in any level of communication, including the edge level (i.e., GED communicates to a local controller) and the system level (i.e., local controllers communicate to the utility's central controller). An Attention-based Long-Short Term Memory (ALSTM) is proposed to build a reference model that enables combining the received redundant data. The proposed approach is implemented on the IEEE 33-bus test system running on a real-time Hardware-In-the-Loop testbed. The proposed approach is validated on an actual battery storage system, as part of the test system, while communicating to its local controller via multiple redundant paths. The results illustrate that the proposed framework significantly reduces the impact of FDIA on the limited number of redundant communication paths in real-time operation.

title: Mathematical Framework for Harmonic Analysis of Cluster Stream Buffer Switching in MMC HVDC: Chebyshev-Based Approach and Insulation
abstract: This paper presents a novel analytical framework for harmonic characterization of the Cluster Stream Buffer (CSB) switching method in Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC)-based Voltage Source Converters (VSCs). Due to the nonlinear nature of Nearest Level Control (NLC), conventional Fourier-based approaches are not well suited for harmonic analysis of CSB. To address this limitation, a Chebyshev polynomial-based method is proposed, enabling a closed-form representation of harmonic components as functions of the modulation index and switching level. The proposed approach provides improved analytical insight and computational efficiency compared to conventional methods. Furthermore, a design methodology integrating harmonic analysis with dielectric stress evaluation is introduced for optimal switching level selection. The results show that a minimum of 33 levels is required under typical conditions, while higher levels (e.g., 49 levels) may be necessary under increased harmonic stress.

title: Temperature-Based Hybrid Modeling for Heating Power Prediction and Fault Detection in Power Transformers
abstract: Accurate estimation of internal heating power is essential for transformer thermal assessment and fault diagnosis. However, the multi-physics coupling and nonlinear heat transfer in oil-immersed transformers make it difficult to infer heating power directly from external temperatures using purely physical models. This paper proposes a hybrid temperature-based framework that integrates physical understanding with data-driven learning. The physical thermal–electrical model is used to reveal the nonlinear temperature–power relationships, guiding feature selection via mutual information (MI) analysis. Selected temperature features are then applied to a random forest (RF) regressor for heating power prediction. Experiments on a thermally equivalent scaled prototype of a 500 kV power transformer, involving 28 operating cases under both normal and fault conditions, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high prediction accuracy, with an average test $R^{2}$ of 0.9956 and a test mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 2.27%. Moreover, deviations in predicted heating power under constant load effectively indicate localized thermal anomalies. The results demonstrate that the proposed hybrid approach offers a practical and interpretable solution for transformer condition monitoring using only external temperature measurements.

title: Application of Impedance-Based Frequency-Dependent System Strength Assessment for Inverter-Dominated Power Systems
abstract: The increasing penetration of inverter-based resources in Great Britain's power system has resulted in a decline in system strength, which has given rise to sub-synchronous oscillations. Traditional methods of assessing system strength are inadequate for system operators to mitigate these oscillations, and therefore, new system strength assessment methods are needed. This paper presents the design of an end-to-end small-signal system strength monitoring process using online impedance measurements, developed through collaborative efforts of a consortium of industry and research partners. The process is based on the evaluation of frequency-dependent impedances from grid measurement data, followed by the computation of a new small-signal system strength metric, Impedance Margin Ratio. Considerations on the feasibility of a practical implementation of the process in a real-world system subject to measurement uncertainty, along with technical aspects such as the injection configuration, are investigated. The process is validated in electromagnetic transient simulations in PSCAD, on a power system model that resembles a high-inverter-dominated region in Great Britain. The results demonstrate that system strength is highly dependent on operating conditions highlighting the importance of evaluating it across multiple system operating scenarios.

title: IGBT Open-Circuit Fault Detection and Localization Method for Cascaded H-Bridge Stage of Power Electronic Transformer
abstract: The rectifier stage of power electronic transformers (PETs) commonly employs either a cascaded H-bridge (CHB) or a modular multilevel converter (MMC) topology. Due to its high modularity, scalability, and ease of redundancy design, the CHB topology is widely adopted in PETs. However, the use of numerous power electronic devices in PETs increases the probability of faults. In this paper, a novel fault detection and localization method is proposed for the rapid identification of IGBT open-circuit faults in the CHB stages of PETs. A mathematical model of the CHB grid-side voltage is established, which contains abundant harmonic information. The harmonic characteristics of the grid-side voltage under different IGBT open-circuit faults are analyzed, revealing that the amplitude and phase of even-order carrier frequency harmonics depend on the location of the faulty H-bridges. Based on this characteristic, the fault region is identified. By adjusting the modulation scheme of specific H-bridges and analyzing the resulting variations in the grid-side voltage, multiple IGBT open-circuit faults can be accurately localized. The proposed method utilizes the characteristic harmonics of the H-bridge port theoretical voltage as a reference, thereby reducing fault-identification time and remaining unaffected by load conditions. Its effectiveness is validated through PSCAD/EMTDC simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments.

title: Transient Response Analysis and System Fault Ride-Through Capability Optimization of HVDC Based on Hybrid Commutated Converter
abstract: Modifying the inverter of line-commutated converter-based high-voltage direct current (LCC-HVDC) to hybrid commutated converter (HCC) is currently a highly effective solution for mitigating the risk of commutation failure (CF). This paper investigates the transient performance of HCC from five perspectives while retaining the LCC-HVDC control system. Since constant extinction angle (CEA) controller leads to significant reduction in power transmission, constant voltage (CV) controller is considered a more appropriate choice as the main controller during AC faults. In addition, the extreme case of insufficient forced commutation capacity leading to CF is considered. It is revealed for the first time that the voltage clamping effect of the arrester will cause a new CF phenomenon. There will be no short circuit on the DC side and the fault current is greatly reduced. This leads to insufficient regulation capability of the CV controller, resulting in continuous CFs. Given the limited fault ride-through capability of the selected CV controller, this paper proposes an adaptive order regulation control (AORC) based on expected reactive power. It can adjust the DC current and voltage in a targeted manner according to AC faults, and determine the maximum allowable upper limit of the firing angle. This improves the reliability of HCC in resisting CF. Under extreme cases, it also effectively prevents the continuous CFs. The simulation results in PSCAD/EMTDC verify the the effectiveness of theoretical analyses and the proposed control method.

title: A Novel Eigenvalue Structure for Two-Mode Resonance Stability Analysis: SSCIs Between Wind Generation and Power Systems as Examples
abstract: Intensified interactions among diversified devices, especially those for wind generation, have caused many events of subsynchronous control interactions (SSCIs) and posed a challenge to power system stability. It is hard for the classical modal analysis to quantify the interaction among oscillation modes explicitly and explain why the interaction or resonance occurs, because eigenvalues and eigenvectors are not differentiable at the resonance point and move drastically nearby. This paper proposes a novel inherence-interaction eigenvalue structure that manages to extend classical single-mode analysis to two-mode resonance stability and SSCI analysis. In the proposed structure, slow-varying inherent eigenvalues denoting properties of two modes themselves and quantities reflecting their interaction are detached. Hence, the SSCI instability mechanism can be ascribed to and explicitly quantified by damping exchange between two modes under interaction. Variation of the oscillation frequency and eigenvectors can be explained likewise. The proposed theory is used to explain SSCI mechanism between wind generation and power systems, and accurately predict rapidly-changing eigenvalues as well as construct the SSCI stability region under parameter variation. The effectiveness is validated by results on two typical systems and the New England 39-bus system, compared with several existing methods.

title: Effects of Deformation of Outer Sheath on Temperature Field and Thermal Circuit Parameters for 110 kV XLPE Cable
abstract: The outer sheath serves as the primary barrier for insulation and protection in a cable. The temperature detection method provides a direct reflection of cable faults, accurate understanding of the cable temperature distribution is a fundamental prerequisite for diagnosing cable issues. This paper first establishes and validates an electromagnetic-thermal coupled finite element (FEM) model of a 110 kV high-voltage (HV) cable installed in an air-filled cable trench. After validating the arc-shaped rectangular minimum bounding box (MBB) model against representative deformation geometries, the study systematically investigates the effects of deformation parameters (angle, depth, and length) on cable temperature distribution. Finally, based on the cable thermal model, the study explores the influence of deformation on the outer sheath's thermal resistance and proposes a correction to the IEC 60287 outer sheath thermal resistance formula. The results indicate that changes in the depth of deformation have the most significant impact on the minimum temperature of the deformed outer sheath. Furthermore, a noticeable linear relationship is observed between deformation angle and outer sheath thermal resistance. The modified outer sheath thermal resistance calculation formula exhibits a fitting error of within ±2.5%, enabling accurate calculation of deformed outer sheath thermal resistance for condition monitoring applications in cable trench installations.

title: Multiple Regulation Phase Shifting Transformer: A Flexible and High-accuracy Power Flow Controller
abstract: With the increasing share of renewable energy in modern power systems, the power grid urgently needs effective power flow regulation technology. The phase shifting transformer has the advantages of strong power flow regulation capability, low investment, high reliability, but the traditional phase shifting transformer can only realize discrete regulation, with low regulation accuracy and lack of appropriate amplitude regulation capability. Therefore, this paper proposes a multiple regulating phase shifting transformer (MR-PST) and its design scheme for power system, analyzes its input and output characteristics based on its topology, examines the nature and distribution of its compensation voltage, and establishes boundary equations from the constraints of single amplitude regulation and dual phase regulation, proving that this structure can effectively increase the number of regulation points, increase the regulation accuracy, introduce the amplitude regulation capability, and optimize the regulation region. Then the power flow regulation region is quantitatively analyzed, and the extremum expression and boundary calculation method of power flow regulation range under different conditions are obtained. Finally, the rationality and practicality of MR-PST were verified through virtual simulation and physical experiments.

title: Perspective and Attribute-Based Self-Supervised Conditional GAN for Few-Shot Bolt Defect Image Generation and Classification
abstract: The scarcity of bolt defect samples in transmission lines presents significant challenges for classification and detection tasks. To address this issue, this paper proposes a Perspective and Attribute-based Self-supervised Conditional Generative Adversarial Network, aiming to enhance the generative capability of few-shot bolt defect images. First, a label generator based on Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training is proposed for automatic bolt perspective division, which autonomously assigns perspective labels to a bolt dataset to alleviate the issue of visual discrepancies. Then, the perspective and attribute information as conditional guides in the generator is introduced to increase the controllability of generation, and a Residual Skip-Layer Excitation is proposed to enhance the gradient information flow. Finally, the U-Net Self-supervised Reconstruction Discriminator is proposed, and a unique local cropping technique named Shape-crop is designed specifically for T-shaped bolts, thereby enhancing the bolts’ feature extraction capability and texture detail generation ability. We constructed a few-shot bolt defect dataset and conducted experiments on it. The experimental results indicate that the method proposed in this paper can generate high-quality bolt defect images and assist in enhancing the accuracy of bolt defect classification, which validates the effectiveness of the methodology presented herein.

title: Stray Current Mitigation With Reverse Running Rail Current Control Strategy for Virtual-Return-Based DC Traction Power Supply System
abstract: The virtual-return-based DC traction power supply system (VRTPS) has been studied to solve the stray current and rail potential issues in urban rail transit. By utilizing the power electronic devices (PEDs) and return line, VRTPS constructs the zero-resistance virtual return path (VRP) by diverting traction current from the running rail into this newly established path. However, the mitigation performance of existing VRTPS control strategies is still suboptimal, leading to incomplete suppression of stray current and rail potential within the train-occupied section. Thus, the reverse running rail current control strategy of VRTPS is proposed to further reduce the stray current and rail potential. Firstly, the topology and modeling of VRTPS are investigated to analyze the inherent limitations of the ideal zero-resistance VRP. Secondly, the detailed analysis of the reverse running rail current control for VRTPS is presented, which optimizes the running rail current distribution with the variable-resistance VRP. Thirdly, the comparative researches on both the stray current and rail potential distribution are conducted between the conventional system and VRTPS with different control strategies. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of VRTPS with proposed strategy on the stray current and rail potential mitigation are validated through simulation and experimental results.

title: Harmonic-Preserved Average-Value Model for Converters in Electromagnetic Transient Simulation
abstract: The increasing utilization of power electronic devices has heightened the impact of harmonics in modern power systems. However, compared with detailed models, conventional average-value models (AVMs) result in reduced accuracy due to the neglect of switching harmonics, making it challenging to meet the accuracy requirements when focusing on transient responses or harmonic dynamics. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a system-level converter model called the harmonic-preserved AVM (HP-AVM). This time-domain-based model integrates AVM computation with harmonic component calculation into a unified simulation framework, enabling precision comparable to that of switching-function models (SFMs) for system-level simulation, while avoiding the high computational burden of detailed models. By leveraging AVMs as the backbone and preserving harmonic details, HP-AVM achieves both high computational efficiency and accurate harmonic representation in system-level simulations. Furthermore, HP-AVM demonstrates broad applicability across various converter topologies, including rectifiers, inverters, and choppers. Both simulation and experimental results validate the effectiveness of HP-AVM, demonstrating its high accuracy and computational efficiency.

title: “High-Impedance Fault Detection” Revisited: Why the Term Has Lost Its Meaning and Should Be Abandoned
abstract: “High-impedance fault” is a commonly used term in power system literature with a decades-long history. While the term may be commonly used, it is not used consistently. This is especially true when one considers the disparity between usage in academic and industry contexts. In academic literature, the term is seldom defined explicitly, but appears to mean something like, “faults that are hard to detect.” When the authors informally survey practitioners, a common answer to the question, “What is a high-impedance fault?” resembles, “It is a fault with a high impedance.” While this is correct by way of tautology, it is unhelpful as a functional matter. Few practitioners or academics include multiple varieties of power system events that occur on operational circuits which might reasonably be called a high impedance fault, nor do they consider distinct and often differing characteristics of such events. Said differently, “high-impedance fault” is not a homogeneous class of events which can be considered uniformly, but a diverse set of power system conditions which share some characteristics and diverge substantially in others. This paper draws on over 40 years of practical experience and research in electrical characterization of normal and abnormal power system transients performed at the Power System Automation Laboratory at Texas A&M University to argue that the term “high-impedance fault” itself has become an impediment to developing techniques and technologies for detecting and mitigating a wide class of power system events which do not reliably operate conventional overcurrent protection devices.

title: Lightning Surge Analysis for DC Direct-Mounted Battery Energy Storage System in MMC-HVDC System
abstract: –Lightning surge overvoltages in a DC direct-mounted battery energy storage system (DCDM-BESS) integrated into a ±500 kV MMC-HVDC link are investigated. An electromagnetic transient (EMT) time-domain model with high-frequency representations of the DCDM-BESS and station equipment is developed to analyze three representative lightning strike scenarios, including tower-strike-initiated metallic return wire (MRW) flashover, direct strikes to the overhead pole wire (OPW) and direct strikes to the MRW. The resulting stress distribution at key measurement points (MPs), including energy storage submodule (ESSM) enclosure-to-ground potentials and the longitudinal voltage across the smoothing reactor (SR), is quantified under different operating modes and MRW installation configurations, and the impact of lightning surge arrester (LSA) arrangements is evaluated. Based on the computed overvoltages, a coordinated protection scheme is proposed, and the required lightning impulse withstand voltages (RLIWV) for ESSM post insulators are derived following an insulation coordination procedure.

title: Analysis of Lightning-Elevated Structures Interaction in Tropical Regions and Implications for Wind Turbine Risk Assessment
abstract: This study analyzes the lightning interaction with elevated structures (ES) in a high-lightning activity region of central Colombia by integrating Lightning Mapping Array (LMA) observations with LINET cloud-to-ground stroke data. In addition, the annual number of lightning flashes (ND) to ES is determined directly from LINET measurements and compared with the obtain using the expression of NTC 4552-2:2023, IEC 62305-2:2024, and the Eriksson equation. The same analysis is extended to two wind farms in northern Colombia, where ND for wind turbines is evaluated following the IEC 61400-24:2018 standard. LMA observations show that all CG strokes affecting ES are initiated by downward leaders and influenced by the lower positive charge region (LPCR) in thunderstorms. Likewise, positive leaders exhibited significantly longer paths than negative leaders. Analysis of ND reveals two exposure regimes: in low-activity regions, structural height governs ND, whereas in high-activity zones the ground flash density (NG) becomes the dominant factor, particularly for ES below 70 m. In general, the ND values obtained from LINET exceed those predicted by the normative formulations. However, using ground strike-point density (NG) values derived directly from the lightning location system (LLS) substantially improves the agreement between calculated and observed ND values, particularly for tall structures and wind turbines, thereby avoiding the underestimation of lightning related design parameters such as the risk components.

title: Dynamic Thermal Line Rating Estimation of Power System
abstract: Dynamic thermal line rating (DTLR) enhances the power transfer capability of thermally limited overhead lines by accounting for real-time environmental and operational conditions. Key influencing factors include solar irradiance, ambient temperature, line current, wind velocity (wind speed with angular direction), and conductor temperature. While some parameters are readily available via online sources or existing sensors, accurate DTLR estimation typically requires wind and conductor temperature data, which often demand additional instrumentation and cost. This paper proposes a cost-effective methodology for short transmission lines that eliminates the need for direct wind and conductor temperature measurements. Instead, it estimates the real-time line resistance using data from emulated SCADA or PMU systems, from which the conductor temperature is subsequently estimated. Using this, along with accessible environmental data, the method estimates wind velocity effects and estimates an optimal DTLR. This method is well suited for regions exhibiting relatively uniform weather conditions, particularly flat terrains. Validation is performed using IEEE Standard 738-2012, with DIgSILENT PowerFactory used to emulate real-time data from SCADA and PMU, and DTLR estimation simulated in MATLAB.

title: Hybrid Grid-Forming Control for Enhanced Active Support and DC Voltage Stability in MMC-HVDC Systems
abstract: Grid-forming control based on power synchronization and DC voltage synchronization is two typical approaches for enabling modular multilevel converter-based high-voltage direct current (MMC-HVDC) systems to operate in weak grids. However, the inherent limitations of their synchronization mechanisms make it difficult to simultaneously ensure system stability and economic efficiency. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a two-stage hybrid grid-forming control strategy. In the first stage, a decoupled matching control is designed to exploit the energy stored in submodule (SM) capacitors for active damping support, which achieves nonlinear indirect matching between DC voltage and frequency while maintaining the economic operation of the sending-end grid. Meanwhile, a voltage stabilization method based on redundant SMs is proposed to decouple SM capacitor voltage from the DC voltage, thereby enhancing DC voltage stability. In the second stage, once the average voltage of the SMs exceeds a predefined threshold, virtual synchronous generator control mobilizes the reserved energy from renewable plants and the rotor kinetic energy of wind turbines, further strengthening inertia and damping support. Moreover, a small signal model is developed to reveal the parameter evolution, and a unified two-stage framework is established through control correction and parameter optimization, thereby improving system dynamic performance and stability. Finally, PSCAD/EMTDC simulations validate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method.

title: Coordination of Directional Overcurrent Relays in Transient Topologies Induced by Faster Operation of Remote-Side Circuit Breakers
abstract: This paper presents a novel methodology for directional overcurrent relays (DOCRs) coordination that effectively accounts for the transient topologies triggered by faster operation of remote-side circuit breakers (CBs), thereby preventing miscoordination and enhancing power system reliability. The methodology is based on the dynamic model of DOCR, allowing for the incorporation of short-circuit currents associated with the moments before and after the operation of remote-side CB in the coordination process. This method facilitates the determination of time multiplier, pickup current, and characteristic curve settings; while earlier methods are unable to determine the latter two settings because updating these settings alters the slope of DOCR curve, shifting the specified interference between DOCRs on both sides of a line to a different fault location. The proposed method is structured as a nested optimization problem: the outer layer establishes the initial operational sequence of DOCRs on both sides of each line, while the inner layer updates the DOCR settings to prevent miscoordination. Comprehensive consideration of various short-circuit types and locations in the study about the faster operation of remote-side CB enhances the robustness of the proposed coordination method compare to existing ones, which is also validated through hardware-in-the-loop testing.

title: Single-terminal Fault Location for Multiterminal HVDCs With Branched Topology
abstract: Research on single-terminal fault locations for multiterminal high-voltage direct current (HVDC) with branched topologies remains limited because i) wave propagation is complicated by impedance discontinuities and line-terminal configurations, hindering universal pattern extraction; and ii) conventional Bergeron method introduces substantial errors for long-distance HVDCs, rendering it unsuitable for single-terminal fault location. To address this, an enhanced Bergeron model (EBM) is first proposed. Frequency-specific propagation delays and losses are incorporated through the Laplace transform and computational circuit inversion. Then, the time-reassigned multi-synchrosqueezing transform (TMSST) processes the guessed wave-process (GWP) and actual wave-process (AWP), reconstructing multi-frequency current waves to label wavefront groups. Reconstructed traveling waves are integrated via weighted least squares (WLS) for robustness. Finally, single-terminal fault location is achieved by optimizing fault distance and fault resistance variables to minimize errors between GWP and AWP. Accurate single-terminal fault location is confirmed in Kunliulong three-terminal HVDC. Without using potential transformers, the method requires only a 2-ms time window and operates reliably under strong noise interferences (with a signal-to-noise ratio as low as 25 dB). Without random forest (RF) correction, non-dead-zone faults show 0.74%-2.81% errors, while dead-zone faults maintain practical applicability with ≤4.22% error. After RF incorporation, the error stays below 0.2% regardless of fault locations.

title: Active Harmonic Voltage Injection Facilitating Application of Impedance Measurement-Based Protection in Microgrids
abstract: A capable and cost-effective protection scheme is essential for the reliable operation of a microgrid. Conventional impedance measurement-based protection is hindered by shorter line lengths, lower line reactance-to-resistance ratios, and fault ride-through (FRT) of inverter-interfaced distributed generators (IIDGs) in microgrids. They are prone to malfunction due to the remote end infeed current during non-metallic faults. This paper addresses this challenge through the coordination of control and protection. IIDGs are configured to actively inject a small harmonic voltage component into the microgrid after fault while coping with FRT requirements using a dual-frequency controller. A hybrid injection activation criterion is embedded to ensure coordinated harmonic injection and equal participation from all IIDGs. Consequently, a uniform harmonic-frequency voltage potential can be generated throughout the microgrid, and its impact on IIDGs' FRT is minimized. The feasibility of the proposed scheme is verified on a hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experimental platform, and its enhancement to protection performance is validated through theoretical and simulation studies. It is revealed that the proposed control scheme can significantly reduce the fault location error and facilitate the application of single-ended impedance measurement-based protection in microgrids.

title: An Efficient Unified-Structure Modeling Method for Hybrid MMCs Based on Subdivision States
abstract: Hybrid modular multilevel converters (MMCs), which integrate multiple types of submodules (SMs), exhibit complex switching behaviors and diverse operational states. These characteristics substantially increase the computational burden in electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation and pose significant challenges for real-time implementation. While existing Thevenin-equivalent models strike a reasonable balance between accuracy and efficiency, their coarse representation of SM states limits further gains in computational performance and hinders extension to new SM topologies, as each requires a topology-specific companion circuit. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an efficient, unified-structure EMT modeling method for hybrid MMCs based on refined SM state decomposition. The proposed approach simplifies the internal equivalent circuits while preserving detailed switching characteristics, enabling a unified mathematical formulation applicable to arbitrary SM types without reconstructing companion circuits. Comparative studies against detailed models in PSCAD demonstrate that the proposed method achieves an accuracy higher than 99.9% while significantly reducing computation time. Furthermore, real-time hybrid digital-physical simulation experiments are conducted on a multi-core CPU platform, benchmarked against the Chongqing-Hubei MMC-HVDC project. Both steady-state power transmission tests and transient power-step experiments confirm that the proposed model completes simulations within a 50μs time step without overruns, while maintaining deviations within approximately 5% compared to field-recorded waveforms.

title: Robust Protection Coordination of Directional Over-Current Relays in AC Microgrids
abstract: Conventional protection coordination in AC microgrids often assumes a single network topology to determine optimal settings for Directional Over-Current Relays (DOCRs), leading to miscoordinations when unconsidered scenarios arise. Unlike previous schemes considering various network scenarios, this paper introduces a novel two-stage protection coordination scheme for DOCRs in an AC microgrid using a robust optimization approach to address the above limitation, wherein the first stage determines two optimal DOCRs settings, one each for Grid-Connected Mode (GCM) and Islanded Mode (IM), and the associated dual variables. The second stage identifies the worst-case scenarios for each DOCR pair, including line and Distributed Generator (DG) outages, varying DGs' injections, and resistive faults, each in GCM and IM. The proposed approach significantly reduces the protection coordination constraints required to obtain the settings, thereby reducing solver execution time and improving computational efficiency. Extensive tests on modified IEEE $13-$bus and IEEE $34-$bus AC microgrids with synchronous and inverter-interfaced DGs, and comparison with previous schemes underscore the reliability of the proposed approach under diverse AC microgrid operating conditions.

title: Cable Shield Grounding for Transient Overvoltage Testing in Power Generation/Transformer Substations
abstract: Transient Overvoltage (TOV) poses significant safety risks to both substation equipment and personnel. Accurate measurement provides an essential reference for overvoltage protection. At present, the outer shield of the test cable used for potential leads is typically grounded at both ends to the ground grid (Method 1) to suppress external magnetic field interference. However, TOV events are usually accompanied by strong Ground Potential Rise (GPR), which causes interference currents on the shield due to Ground Potential Difference (GPD), leading to measurement errors. To address this issue, this paper proposes an alternative grounding scheme in which the outer shield is connected in parallel with a metal return wire (Method 2), thereby mitigating the impact of GPD. A numerical calculation model for evaluating the Shielding Effectiveness (SE) of the test cable under both interference magnetic fields and GPD was developed. The SEs of Method 1 and Method 2 were analyzed in both the frequency domain and under typical transient magnetic field waveforms in the time domain. The results show that, for each GPD frequency, there exists a characteristic interference magnetic field frequency f. When the magnetic field frequency is lower than f, Method 2 achieves significantly higher SE than Method 1; when it is higher than f, the SE of the two methods becomes nearly identical. Under typical magnetic fields, Method 2 consistently outperforms Method 1, with a maximum SE difference of 28 dB observed under a ringing wave condition. In practice, the selection of the test cable shield grounding method during TOV testing at generation and transformer substations should be based on the dominant frequency of the interfering magnetic field and the amplitude and frequency of GPD. For Transient Ground Potential Rise (TGPR) tests, Method 2 is strongly recommended.

title: Large-Scale Multi-Period Optimal Asset Renewal Planning: A Comprehensive and Efficient MILP Approach
abstract: Many electric utilities worldwide are facing critical challenges of cost-effectively renewing aging assets to maintain power network reliability. Existing asset renewal planning (ARP) methods often have limited applicability in complex real-world scenarios, and may fail to capture the synergy between different asset types and the interplay between proactive and reactive renewals. To address these limitations, this paper develops a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP)-based approach for large-scale multi-period ARP. This approach formulates the multi-period ARP problem as an MILP model, which comprehensively accounts for the costs associated with both proactive and reactive asset renewals, regular asset maintenance, and system failures, thus capturing the interplay among them. Real-world limitations in workforce and requirements for system reliability can be conveniently integrated into the constraints of the MILP model. The approach integrates the renewal of all critical asset types, including transformers, switchgears, and cables, into one unified framework, maximizing synergies across them. Moreover, a candidate-selection-based iterative solution method is devised for the MILP model, which ensures computational tractability for large-scale ARP problems. The application of the approach to a real distribution network demonstrates its effectiveness and superiority over the traditional age-based asset renewal planning.

title: Observation and Numerical Calculation of Induced Voltage caused by M component on 10 kV Overhead Distribution Line
abstract: This article analyzes the lightning-induced voltage (LIV) waveforms generated by M-components recorded by rocket-triggered lightning experiments and performs numerical calculations to investigate the impact of variations in M-component process parameters on the LIV waveforms. The LIVs were measured on a vertically arranged, 1513-meter-long, 10 kV three-phase overhead distribution line. Based on the occurrence time of the M-component, the characteristics of the current waveform, and the polarity of the induced voltage, the M-components measured can be classified into three Types. In addition, this study employs the method of controlling variables and utilizes the hybrid MTL-PEEC (Multi-Conductor Transmission Line – Partial Element Equivalent Circuit) model to analyze the influence of M-component parameters on the induced voltage. The results indicate that an increase in the current rise time leads to a decrease in the absolute value of the negative peak of the induced voltage at the nearest pole, while the positive peak and polarity reversal time increase. An increase in the current half-width results in a longer polarity reversal time and extended decay time after the positive peak. A higher ground reflection coefficient causes increases in both the negative and positive peaks of the induced voltage. Furthermore, an increase in channel height leads to a greater absolute value of the negative peak, a decrease in the positive peak, and a delay in the time to reach peak voltage.

title: Novel Series-Capacitor-Type Modular Multilevel Converters to Reduce Capacitor Voltage Ripples Based on Harmonic Injection
abstract: Modular multilevel converter (MMC) has been widely used in DC power transmission, motor control, etc. Sub-modules (SMs) capacitor voltage fluctuation is the main factor affecting the performance and capacitance design of MMC. Besides, harmonic injection is a popular approach to achieve fluctuation suppression of the SMs capacitor voltage, but it is prone to the increase of common-mode voltage. In this paper, a novel series-capacitor-type modular multilevel converter (SCTMMC) is proposed. SCTMMC introduces a new intermediate module between the midpoint of the Traditional MMC arm and the output. With this module, the AC output-side common-mode voltage is eliminated through harmonic injection, the capacitor voltage balance is ensured by a dedicated control scheme, and the quality of the AC current is improved. The effectiveness of the proposed structure and control method in suppressing the arm energy fluctuation is verified by analyzing the mathematical model of SCTMMC. In addition, the SCTMMC has fewer power electronic devices, and the control of the intermediate module is simpler, which showed better compatibility for the improvement of the existing harmonic voltage injection control method. Finally, the performance of SCTMMC was verified by simulation and experiment results.

title: Reduced-scale test method for dynamic responses of bundle conductor line following ice-shedding
abstract: A reduced-scale test method for dynamic responses of bundle conductor line following ice-shedding is proposed. In this method, hollow cylindrical electromagnets are used to absorb and release mass blocks modelling ice on and ice-shedding from sub-conductors, multiple cameras are utilized to capture the vertical, transverse and torsional vibrations, tension sensors to measure tensions in all sub-conductors, and three-component force sensors to measure the reaction force at hanging points. Without simplifying the bundle conductor line into a single one which was employed in previous works, the proposed reduced-scale model can satisfy the similarities of bending and torsion stiffness at the same time, model the torsional vibration induced by ice-shedding from sub-conductors, and record tension in each sub-conductor. Reduced-scale test platform for a twin-bundle conductor line was established and utilized to study the dynamic characteristics of the twin-bundle conductor line following partial, unzipping and asynchronous ice-shedding from sub-conductors. The method can be extended to investigate dynamic characteristics of bundle conductor lines following any pattern of ice-shedding.

title: Design and Verification of Novel Self-Voltage Sharing Vacuum Interrupter for Multi-Break VCBs in GIS
abstract: A key challenge for multi-break vacuum circuit breakers (VCBs) in gas-insulated switchgear (GIS) is the design of compact voltage grading solutions for vacuum interrupters (VIs). This paper addresses the non-uniform voltage distribution across VI shields and series-connected breaks in VCBs that is caused by the significantly increased stray capacitances in GIS. To address these issues, we propose a novel self-voltage sharing capacitor pattern (SSCP), and the equivalent circuit of the VI with SSCP is analyzed. Simulations of the SSCP and the conventional grading capacitor pattern (CGCP) were conducted, and the maximum external electric field strength of the VI with SSCP was reduced by 53.6%, while the temperature rise was also decreased by 33.9%. A 40.5-kV VI prototype with SSCP was developed based on ring capacitors, external shields, and integrated encapsulation. Experimental results for series-connected VIs with SSCP demonstrate that the potential distributions among the shields and breaks approach the ideal values. The withstand voltage of series-connected VIs with SSCP is increased by 12.5%, and the temperature rise is decreased by 32.2%. The feasibility of the VI with SSCP has been verified, providing a compact voltage-sharing design reference for ultra-high-voltage multi-break VCBs in GIS.

title: A Multi-Break Mechanical Switch with High Arc Voltage and Fast Post-Arc Recovery for Hybrid DC Circuit Breakers
abstract: While natural commutation hybrid DC circuit breakers (HCBs) achieve lower conduction losses and cost-effectiveness compared to forced commutation HCBs, their inherently limited arc voltage fundamentally constrains commutation reliability and operational speed. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a multi-break mechanical switch (MBMS) consisting of a fast-recovery break gap in series with multiple arc-voltage-assisted break gaps. The configuration enables rapid post-arc recovery to withstand transient overvoltages while using high arc voltage to ensure stable commutation. When deployed in natural commutation hybrid DC circuit breakers (HCBs), the MBMS provides advantages including low loss, reliable commutation, and cost-effectiveness. Following the presentation of the structure of the MBMS, this paper introduces design methodologies for arc voltage, contact weight, and operational mechanisms. Subsequently, a prototype of the natural commutation HCB utilizing the MBMS is constructed at 10 kV/15 kA. The verification of the correctness of the MBMS structure and design methodologies, along with the demonstration of the effectiveness of this approach in the structure of natural commutation HCBs, is presented.

title: Transient Voltage and Current Calculations Based on Formulation of Modified Baum-Liu-Tesche Equation in Phase Domain
abstract: This study presents a modified Baum-Liu-Tesche (BLT) equation, derived in a compact matrix-algebraic form, for the frequency-domain analysis of transient voltages and currents in multi-conductor transmission lines (MTLs). The proposed formulation addresses two broad categories of transient events, including faults and lightning strikes, while accommodating diverse event types and occurrence scenarios. The modified BLT equation is further extended into an explicit form, enabling its application to power networks with inhomogeneous parameters and complex topologies. This extension is supported by a systematic derivation of the structural features and element characteristics of the involved matrices and vectors. Numerical validation using the benchmark IEEE 34-bus test distribution network confirms strong agreement between the results obtained from the modified BLT equation and those generated by electromagnetic-transient-type simulations. Overall, the proposed formulation provides an effective and robust analytical framework for transient analysis in power systems.

title: Multirate EMT Simulation of Power Electronic Transformers With High-Precision Firing Signals
abstract: The electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation of power electronic transformers (PETs) encounters significant computational challenges due to the high switching frequency nature imposing small simulation time step. This paper proposes a multirate simulation method incorporating high-precision firing signals, which enhances the simulation efficiency of PETs by reducing the number of numerical operations within specified simulation durations. Unlike the existing methods that utilize simplified models with unanimous simulation time step, the proposed approach leverages the inherent frequency disparities in multi-level conversion circuits of PETs to partition the entire system into distinct subsystems. They each are simulated with different time steps optimized for their specific frequencies and precision requirements. To achieve the coordination between subsystems with different rates while ensuring simulation stability, a simulation data transmission method for different subsystems and an interleaved equivalence multirate interaction algorithm are developed. By formulating the currents on both sides of the high frequency transformer as state variables, which are derived by modified nodal analysis (MNA), high-precision firing signals are introduced achieving significant time step enlargement in high frequency subsystem. The performance of the proposed method is validated through comparative studies with traditional single rate (TSR) EMT simulations under various operating conditions.

title: A Cutting-Edge Device for DC Fault Isolation and Enhanced AC/DC Fault Ride-Through for MTDC Systems —PART II: Verification and Comparisons
abstract: This two-part paper proposes a device that integrates dc fault isolation with ac/dc fault ride-through capacities. A four-terminal MTDC simulation system and a simplified low-voltage hardware experimental platform are established for demonstrating the functions of clearing the dc fault current and dissipating surplus power. The experimental results are compared with those of a simulation to analyze the feasibility of the proposed device and verify the reliability of the simulation. Using the simulation system, the proposed device competes against representative dc circuit breaker (DCCB) schemes with dc chopper schemes. The proposed device can effectively clear dc fault current and dissipate the surplus power. The proposed device lowers the cost of components by at least 33.7% from those of independently configured DCCBs with dc choppers.

title: A Novel Transient Disturbance Waveform Compression Method in Distribution Networks Based on Dictionary Learning
abstract: The distribution network with a large-scale integration of distributed renewable energy sources exhibits more complex dynamic behavior. The widespread deployment of high-resolution waveform monitoring in distribution networks is hindered by the massive data transmission and storage requirements. To mitigate this communication bottleneck, this paper proposes a novel transient disturbance waveform compression method in distribution networks based on dictionary learning. A new framework for disturbance waveform compression on terminal side and reconstruction on master station side has been proposed to outline the offline learning and online decomposition steps. Then a determination method of the start and end times of transient disturbance waveforms based on the relative energy acceleration operator (REAO) has been proposed for disturbance waveform segmentation, which clarifies the disturbance processes that need to be monitored. To improve the decomposition and reconstruction efficiency, an overcomplete dictionary design method that considers feature redundancy within the dictionary based on clustering pruning optimized K SVD (CPK-SVD) has been proposed. The redundant atoms in the dictionary are pruned based on Gaussian mixture model (GMM) clustering method after feature extraction. Simulation and field recorded waveform data tests show that the proposed method can achieve a compression ratio of over 10 while ensuring measurement accuracy.

title: A Segmented Insulation Assessment Method of Power Cable Based on EWV Inversion
abstract: Compared with the traditional holistic insulation assessment (HIA) methods, which can only provide the insulation condition information of whole cables, segmented insulation assessment (SIA) can provide the insulation condition information of each cable segment, thereby enhancing cable maintenance efficiency. In the past, SIA was achieved by estimating the attenuation coefficient through quantitatively calculating reflected wave amplitudes. However, multiple signal reflections within the cable cause cross-coupling among reflected wave amplitudes, leading to poor generalizability and inaccuracy in SIA. In this article, an SIA method based on velocity inversion using compressive subspace multiple signal classification (CS-MUSIC) is proposed to avoid the problem of the past method. The idea of the proposed method is that electromagnetic wave velocity (EWV) in a power cable is associated with the insulation condition of the cable. The more serious the cable insulation aging, the slower the EWV. Besides, a power cable can naturally be divided into several segments by power cable joints. Consequently, if the EWV in each cable segment can be assessed, the EWV can be used to evaluate the insulation condition of each cable segment. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified through simulation, experiment, and a 10kV power cable field test.

title: Partial Discharge Identification and Area Location in Transformer Based on Multi-Terminal Polarity
abstract: Partial discharge identification and location are critical for ensuring the safe operation of transformers. High frequency current monitoring, known for its ease of installation and high sensitivity, is widely used for online partial discharge monitoring in transformers. This technique typically identifies the initial waveform polarity to locate the partial discharge source. However, the presence of electromagnetic noise in field environments poses a significant challenge to accurately identify the initial waveform polarity, resulting in difficulties in both the identification and location of partial discharges. To address these challenges, this paper investigates the signal propagation characteristics and polarity features of partial discharges in transformers using the full-winding circuit model. A waveform polarity-based method for partial discharge identification and location is proposed, consisting of two components: a waveform polarity identification approach utilizing principal component analysis (PCA), and a multi-terminal waveform polarity criterion for partial discharge location. Finally, the proposed method is validated through partial discharge detection experiments conducted on a 500 kV transformer. It was demonstrated that the polarity identification accuracy reached 97.78%, with the detected multi-terminal polarity patterns conforming to the established criterion for locating partial discharges. This paper provides an effective technical basis for accurate partial discharge location in transformers.

title: Flexible Voltage Source Grounding Based Active Arc Suppression Technique for Large-Scale Wind Farm Considering All Collector Lines
abstract: Wind farm collector line single-line ground (SLG) fault arcs are difficult to suppress, which severely threatens the safety of wind farm operations. For this reason, an active arc suppression technique based on flexible voltage source grounding is proposed. A composite sequence network model of a wind farm collector line SLG fault is theoretically deduced. The mechanism of the influence of faulted and nonfaulted collector line wind turbine output currents and collector line impedance on fault residual currents is analyzed. By connecting a controllable voltage source in parallel at the neutral point of the wind farm, the amplitude and phase of the positive-sequence equivalent potential (PSEP) of the wind farm are actively searched and calculated, and the faulty phase voltage of the wind farm can be suppressed to zero. Thus, the ground fault current is eliminated, and arc suppression of wind farm ground faults is realized. A large wind farm with a double-fed induction generator (DFIG) is modeled using PSCAD/EMTDC, and various system operating conditions and ground fault conditions are simulated. The results show that the proposed methods can effectively suppress the fault point voltage of wind farm collector lines, reliably eliminate the fault residual current, and achieve grounding fault arc suppression under different operating and fault conditions.

title: Operating Temperature Analysis of Dry-Type Capacitors Under Superimposed AC-DC Voltage
abstract: Dry-type capacitors, which have high operating voltage and energy storage density, have been widely used in VSC-HVDC, but the complex electrical and thermal environments pose significant challenges to the operational stability of capacitors. It is difficult to directly measure the temperature distribution inside capacitors, and existing computation models simulate capacitor components as equivalent series resistance, ignoring the temperature dependence and electric field dependence of capacitor models under complex electrothermal condition. This paper focuses on the biaxially oriented polypropylene (BOPP) capacitors, considering its dielectric characteristics under superimposed AC-DC voltage and high ambient temperature, quantitatively describes the temperature dependence and electric field dependence of the BOPP's leakage current and dielectric losses. A finite element electrothermal coupling model considering the characteristics of dielectric materials is proposed, and the temperature distribution of capacitors under the superimposed AC-DC voltage is obtained, the influence of ambient temperature and dielectric properties on the thermoelectric coupling of capacitor is analyzed. This work provides a guidance for the material and structure design of capacitors.

title: Contour Optimization of DC-GIS Insulator Considering the Influence of Surface Charging Withstanding Transient Voltages
abstract: Surface charging on insulator in DC-GIS is influenced by transient voltages like lightning impulse (LI) and polarity reversal (PR), which threatens the safe operation of the equipment. In this paper, a contour optimization method considering the influence of surface charging is proposed for insulator used in DC-GIS of ±320 kV. The insulation reliability under steady DC voltage is promoted, and the property to withstand the transient voltages is guaranteed as well. The normal and tangential components of electric field under steady DC voltage are simultaneously minimized, and the constraints on electric field under the transient voltages are incorporated. The results show that, under the steady DC voltage, the maximal value of normal electric field is reduced by 5.8%, and the tangential field is simultaneously reduced by 7.0% on the insulator with the optimal contour after optimization. The maximal values of electric fields under the LI and PR voltages are 8.82 and 3.49 kV/mm, respectively, meeting the insulation requirements. It is suggested that, the proposed method incorporating the property withstanding the LI and PR voltages yields a more reliable performance of the optimized insulator in DC-GIS.

title: Thermoelectric-Driven Conduction Mechanisms of Carbon-Ceramic Closing Resistors in Circuit Breakers Under Pulsed-Energy Injection
abstract: Closing resistors are critical components in ultra-high-voltage circuit breakers, however, their dynamic conduction under pulsed-energy injection remains poorly understood, thereby limiting energy-handling capability and compromising breaker reliability. This study combines pulsed-energy injection experiments and thermoelectrically coupled simulations to elucidate the electrothermal response and conductivity evolution of carbon-ceramic resistors. By correlating macroscopic resistance variations with microscopic conductive-chain dynamics, the conduction process is divided into four distinct stages: transient conduction, sustained decline, steady fluctuation, and gradual recovery. A thermoelectric-driven mechanism governing the conductive network is proposed. The microscale network consists of non-conductive, discontinuous, and continuous conductive chains, whose activation is jointly controlled by both the electric field and temperature. Strong electric fields induce tunneling conduction in discontinuous chains, whereas thermal expansion effectively reduces contact resistance in continuous chains. The individual and coupled influences of temperature and electric field are quantified by numerical fitting of the recovery resistance versus temperature and transient resistance versus field. Results reveal a pronounced thermoelectric synergy with clear energy dependence. Under low-energy injection, coupling enhances carrier excitation, yielding resistance reductions exceeding the sum of individual thermal and electrical contributions. Under high-energy injection, conductive-chain saturation suppresses further synergy, leading to smaller-than-additive resistance reductions.

title: Deriving a Novel Equivalent Circuit to Capture Current Transformer Behavior Under Partial Saturation Phenomena Caused by Stray Fluxes
abstract: Presence of the external stray fluxes or eccentric installation of the primary conductor results in non-uniform flux distribution in the current transformer (CT) core. This causes saturation in some portions of the core, called partial saturation (PS) phenomenon. Moreover, the saturation of the entire core results in CT total saturation. In both cases, CT accuracy decreases, which can result in measurement and tariff meter inaccuracy as well as protective relay maloperation. In this article, a novel electrical equivalent circuit is derived to accurately model stray fluxes and eccentricity of the primary conductor effects on partial and total saturation phenomena. The method is based on dividing the CT iron core into some portions. Each portion is then modeled with a nonlinear inductance within the equivalent circuit. This approach accurately captures the behavior of the CT under the PS phenomenon. The method demonstrates remarkable accuracy, closely mirroring outcomes obtained through finite element method (FEM) simulations and practical experimentations, and shows a significant speedup by a factor of 100 compared to the FEM. The ability to model stray fluxes and PS phenomena, along with high efficiency, makes the new circuit model very useful and necessary for implementing in electromagnetic transient program simulation tools.
