title: Adaptive Hybrid Prediction-Correction With Trust-Region and Dynamic Line Search for AC/DC Load Flow
abstract: Hybrid AC/DC power systems are gaining importance due to the rising penetration of Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) and the widespread deployment of Voltage Source Converters (VSCs). Analyzing power flow in such systems remains challenging due to unbalanced operating conditions, strong nonlinearities, and strict operational limits. This paper presents an Adaptive Hybrid Prediction–Correction algorithm with Trust-Region and Dynamic Line Search (AHPC-TRDLS) for reliable and efficient load flow computation in large-scale hybrid systems. The framework couples a Newton–Raphson-based prediction stage with a Preconditioned Conjugate Gradient (PCG) correction, bounded adaptively by a trust-region radius. A dynamic line search mechanism is incorporated as a fallback whenever the PCG convergence stalls, ensuring numerical stability. Additional features include adaptive preconditioning, enforcement of voltage and reactive power limits, and the use of symmetrical components for unbalanced system modeling. The algorithm is implemented in MATLAB and evaluated on different hybrid AC/DC test systems of varying scales. Case studies confirm that the proposed approach offers improved convergence, robustness, and scalability under stressed, ill-conditioned, and unbalanced scenarios.

title: Effect of IBR Negative-Sequence Control on Phase-to-Phase Fault Direction Determination
abstract: Protective relays implement algorithms to determine the direction to the fault. Phase-to-phase fault detection, can rely on negative sequence components. If the negative sequence currents provided by an inverter-based resource (IBR) are not reliable, the directional determination of the fault is not consistent. In this paper, we compare two types of IBRs: grid-following (GFL) and grid-forming (GFM), for their dynamic performance when subject to phase-to-phase faults on the high side of the step-up transformer. The GFL-IBR behaves as a positive-sequence current source, while the GFM-IBR behaves as a voltage source behind an inductive impedance in the positive-sequence circuit, and as an inductive impedance in the negative-sequence circuit. It is found that the GFM-IBR ensures proper fault ride-through, while the GFL-IBR cannot ride through such a fault. Additionally, the GFM-IBR ensures correct fault detection via negative-sequence directionality check, while this check fails for the GFL-IBR case. Therefore, the GFM design presented in this paper appears to have two advantages compared to the legacy GFL design: better capability of fault ride-through and assurance of correct fault direction determination.

title: Research on Infeeder Line Protection Scheme for Traction Substation Under Bilateral Power Supply Mode
abstract: The infeeder line of the traction substation(TS) serves as a critical transmission link connecting the power system and the electrified railway, and an effective protection scheme is of immense importance for the stable operation of both systems. The fault mechanisms and characteristics of the infeeder line under the bilateral power supply mode(BPSM) differ significantly from those under the conventional unilateral power supply mode(UPSM). However, existing research lacks a thorough discussion of infeeder protection under BPSM. This article establishes protection criteria based on local voltage and current, and proposes an exhaustive scheme capable of comprehensively revealing the characteristics of all fault types across various operational scenarios. The proposed scheme is simple to implement, operates independently of synchronous communication and avoids issues such as insufficient sensitivity and relay settings coordination conflicts caused by weak short circuit current feed effects. Additionally, it exhibits strong robustness and can reliably distinguishes potential transformer(PT) failure, regenerative braking energy feedback, and the TS on the healthy side. Finally, simulation results based on actual parameters verify the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed protection scheme.

title: The Effect of Airflow on the Flashover Voltage and Path of Roof Insulators
abstract: As the operating speed of high-speed trains continues to rise, roof insulators are subjected to strong airflow for prolonged periods, significantly influencing their discharge behavior. To investigate how airflow affects the flashover characteristics of roof insulators, this study conducts flashover voltage tests and captures discharge paths in a wind tunnel using a scaled model. Combined with computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations, the study systematically analyzes the leeward flow field at various inlet wind speeds and its effects on flashover paths and voltages. The results show that as wind speed increases, the flashover voltage initially rises, then decreases, and finally stabilizes. Meanwhile, the flashover path first moves away from the insulator and then approaches it, reflecting the nonlinear influence of the aerodynamic environment on both the arc path and flashover voltage. Airflow generates pronounced negative pressure and recirculation zones on the leeward side of the insulator. As wind speed increases, the negative pressure and recirculating flow intensify and move closer to the insulator surface, significantly altering the arc force direction and discharge path. At low wind speeds, the arc extends downstream and is blown away, whereas at high wind speeds, it is pulled toward the insulator by the recirculating flow. This causes the discharge path to elongate and then shorten, resulting in a corresponding rise followed by a decrease in flashover voltage. This study offers theoretical insights and practical guidance for optimizing insulator design in high-speed trains and understanding aerodynamic discharge mechanisms.

title: Analytical Method for Calculation of Electromagnetic Fields from Armoured HVAC Cables
abstract: With the proliferation of HVAC armoured cables in offshore wind applications, the provision of methods for the calculation of both magnetic and electric field effects from HV cables is of high importance for consenting processes associated with offshore wind development and biological experiments. Despite electro-reception of marine animals being a known phenomenon, the electric fields present outside of HVAC cables, mostly induced as a result of the time-varying magnetic vector potential, have not been thoroughly analysed in literature. The available methods for the calculation of magnetic fields are often complex and require an expert user. In this work, this knowledge gap is addressed through the development of an analytical method, with some parameters derived from simple numerical simulations, that can be applied to both magnetic and electric fields and by provision of MATLAB code for calculation of both effects. The presented method includes the impact of metallic sheaths, cable twist, and magnetic armour. For the development of electric field expressions, the impact of the insulating layer at the cable outer boundary is considered. The presented results are within 3% of the numerical solution for the magnetic and electric field norm and within 5% for the individual components of the fields.

title: Impedance-Spectrum Driven Frequency Weighted Functional Fault Location in Undersea Observation Network Power Systems
abstract: Fault location in the power supply systems of undersea observation networks is constrained by limited observability and the frequency-dependent characteristics of the electrode–seawater–cable loop. This paper proposes a frequency-domain fault location method based on impedance spectrum analysis, in which the identification of fault parameters is formulated as a minimization problem of a frequency-weighted residual functional. A physical model of the electrode–cable–fault path is constructed to compute theoretical input impedance spectra under different fault distances and fault impedances. These spectra are then compared to the measured impedance spectrum obtained at the shore station under swept-frequency excitation. The residual functional is constructed by separating the real and imaginary components of the spectral difference, reflecting the deviation of complex input impedance at each frequency point. Considering the influence of impedance sensitivity across frequencies, independent weighting functions are introduced for the real and imaginary components to enhance contributions from informative bands and suppress unreliable regions. This yields a frequency-weighted residual functional with physical significance, characterizing the correspondence between fault parameters and spectral discrepancy. The functional is minimized via a gradient-based optimization strategy, enabling simultaneous determination of fault distance and fault impedance based solely on shore-side measurements. Simulation studies across various fault conditions validate the method's performance in terms of location accuracy, robustness under high impedance scenarios, and numerical stability over long transmission distances. The proposed framework fuses spectral sensitivity with physical transmission modeling to infer spatial fault characteristics solely from frequency-domain observations, without relying on internal measurements or reflectometry.

title: Non-Unit Protection Based on Transient Voltage Time-Frequency Characteristics for Offshore Flexible Low-Frequency Transmission Lines
abstract: Offshore flexible low-frequency AC transmission (OFLFAC) systems face unique protection challenges due to full-power electronic interfaces and 20 Hz operation modes. To address these challenges, a novel non-unit transient protection method is proposed, utilizing the boundary characteristics of modular multilevel matrix converters (M3C). First, the parameters of three-core submarine cables are decoupled and modal decomposition is applied to analyze the strong attenuation characteristics of high-frequency waves at substation buses and M3C converter boundaries. Next, a noise-immune successive variational mode decomposition algorithm combined with mathematical morphology filtering is designed to separate low-frequency traveling waves from high-frequency transients. A hybrid criterion is proposed: the average slope ratio of low-frequency forward and backward traveling waves identifies the fault direction, while the inner product ratio of high-frequency peak operators distinguishes high-impedance internal faults from external low-impedance faults. Simulation results show that the proposed method can operate reliably within 2.4 ms, withstand transition resistances up to 1000 $\Omega$ and low signal-to-noise ratio environments of 10 dB, and remain unaffected by control strategies, thereby effectively addressing the reliability shortcomings of single-ended protection in complex fault scenarios.

title: Stability Boundary Evaluation Method for the Cascaded Bipolar DC Distribution System With CPLs Based on Impedance Analysis
abstract: At present, most existing methods for suppressing voltage oscillations induced by constant power loads (CPLs) in bipolar DC distribution systems (Bi-DCDSs) only focus on control frameworks, while the evaluation of the CPL power demand boundary defined by control parameters for ensuring system stability remains unexplored. To help tuning the control parameters, this paper proposes a boundary evaluation method to support control parameter tuning and thereby ensure the stability of Bi-DCDSs. The methods for suppressing voltage oscillations discussed in this paper include: the virtual impedance control (VIC) method based on the positive and negative port components, and the VIC method based on the DC symmetrical components. Firstly, the source impedance models and load admittance models of the Bi-DCDS controlled by the two VIC methods are established. Based on these established models, the input-output gain matrices of the Bi-DCDS are derived, providing foundation for stability analysis. Using the Generalized Nyquist Criterion, the stability of a Bi-DCDS with specified parameters can be assessed. By exploring the stability of the Bi-DCDS under different CPL power demands, the boundary can be identified. The case study demonstrates that, for a ±375 V system, the evaluation results obtained by the proposed method deviate from the simulation-identified boundary by less than 2 kW, verifying the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: BF-YOLO:GIS Inner Surface Detection Model based on an improved YOLOv8
abstract: Gas insulated switchgear (GIS) equipment, a crucial component of power grids, requires regular maintenance to ensure stable operation. However, traditional inspection methods have limitations in detecting internal surface defects in GIS pipes, potentially resulting in inefficiencies and safety risks. This paper proposes BF-YOLO, an improved method for internal surface defect detection based on YOLOv8, to address this challenge. BF-YOLO utilizes ShapeIoU loss to focus on edge shapes and scale, enabling more accurate bounding box regression and enhancing detection precision. The FasterNetBlock module helps reduce the model size for more efficient deployment on embedded devices or mobile platforms. The C2F_Faster module further optimizes parameters and model volume while maintaining detection accuracy. Additionally, the reconstructed neck structure, inspired by BiFPN, expands the model's receptive field and enhances spatial information processing, thereby improving the detection of small targets. Compared to the original YOLO model, BF-YOLO demonstrates significant improvements, with mAP@0.5 increasing by 1.1% while the number of parameters and GFLOPs are reduced by 44.1% and 22.2% respectively. These improvements enable faster and more accurate defect detection in GIS pipelines. BF-YOLO provides a valuable solution for automated defect detection, thereby enabling proactive maintenance and enhancing safety and reliability in power grid operations.

title: Optimal Placement of Dynamic Thermal Rating Considering Transient Temperature of Overhead Lines with Two-Stage Robust Guarantee against N-1 Contingency
abstract: Dynamic thermal rating (DTR) is an economically efficient technique to improve the transmission capacity of existing overhead lines and alleviate transmission congestion caused by high penetration of renewable energy. However, it is still challenging to optimize the DTR placement with security assurance under N-1 contingency, which suffers from the curse of dimensionality in traditional optimization approaches. In this paper, a two-stage robust optimization approach for optimal placement of DTR devices is proposed to improve the transmission capacity of overhead lines. First, a transient temperature calculation model of overhead lines and its simplified approximation are proposed to possess the desirable property of convexity in the following model. Then, a two-stage robust optimization model for optimal placement of DTR devices is developed to avoid the cascading failure or blackout under N-1 contingency. An alternating current optimal power flow model based on second-order cone programming is utilized to calculate the line current more accurately. Case studies on several test systems verify the effectiveness of the proposed method in improving transmission capacity and reducing total cost.

title: Optimization-Based Method for Aggregate Wind and Solar Capacity Estimation and Feeder Power Prediction
abstract: In 2050, clean deep electrification will require the connection of innumerable distributed energy resources (DERs) to power distribution utilities. The current utility practice of requiring complete DER information for operational applications, such as short-term feeder power prediction (FPP), will not be feasible in the future considering innumerable DERs. Unlike existing studies on DER hosting capacity estimation—which focus on determining the maximum DER capacity a system can integrate without grid reinforcements—this study addresses the future challenge of estimating the aggregate capacity (EAC) of connected DERs. Additionally, it aims to forecast the feeder power at the medium-voltage (MV) level. The proposed approach integrates advanced optimization techniques with deep neural network (DNN) models. An optimization method is introduced, where the first stage involves training basic solar and wind DNN models. In the next stages, EAC values for DERs are determined, and a load model is developed. Once the models for DERs and loads are trained and their aggregate capacities are determined, the framework enables real-time short-term FPP by utilizing weather and chronological data as inputs. The proposed model is tested on real utility data, demonstrating an average accuracy of 97.45% for EAC and 97.29% for FPP. A comparison with a direct FPP shows the superiority of the proposed sequential approach.

title: Does Series Compensation Improve the Transient Stability of Inverter-Based Resources?
abstract: Series compensation has long been recognized as a viable solution for improving the transient stability of power systems energized by synchronous machines (SMs). However, the generation fleet is increasingly shifting towards inverter-based resources (IBRs). This shift prompts the question as to whether series compensation can also improve the transient stability of systems with IBRs during grid faults. This paper focuses on wind and solar inverters. These inverters predominantly rely on a phase-locked loop (PLL) for synchronization. Therefore, their transient stability is closely linked to the ability of their PLLs to maintain synchronism with the grid voltage during low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) conditions. The available literature on the transient stability of PLL-based IBRs identifies grid weakness as a primary driver of PLL instability. Grid weakness is characterized mainly by the high inductance of long transmission lines. Series compensation is a well-understood solution for reducing the line inductance. Therefore, at the outset, it seems reasonable to hypothesize that series compensation can enhance the transient stability of systems with IBRs as well. This paper puts this hypothesis to analytical and simulation testing, investigating whether the conventional wisdom on series compensation regarding transient stability always holds in systems with IBRs. We identify previously undocumented destabilizing effects caused by the series capacitor and its protective components. A salient feature of this paper is that its findings are independent of PLL design and parameter selection. The theoretical analyses of this study are substantiated by detailed PSCAD/EMTDC simulations of a weak transmission system reinforced through series compensation.

title: Nonintrusive Distributed Detection Method for GIS Metal Particle Defects based on a ϕ-OTDR
abstract: Optical fibers based on vibroacoustic sensing technology offer significant potential for detecting discharge defects in gas-insulated switchgear (GIS). However, there is a lack of research on multiplexing techniques for optical fiber sensors, which hampers the broader adoption of vibroacoustic sensing in GIS applications. To address this gap, this paper proposes a distributed detection method for metallic particle defects in a GIS based on a phase-sensitive optical time domain reflector (ϕ-OTDR). Building on this method, an optical fiber sensing topology is established; the sensing units are optimally designed, and a full-scale 110 kV GIS metallic particle defect detection test platform is constructed to evaluate the distributed sensing capabilities of the proposed system. The experimental results show that the developed distributed optical fiber sensing system is capable of performing multipoint synchronous detection of GIS partial discharge signals on the order of hundreds of pC. By affixing the sensing units to the exterior surfaces of each chamber shell, the system achieves simultaneous identification of metallic particle defects in 25 chambers during a single test. The findings of this study provide a novel solution for the operation and maintenance of GIS equipment.

title: A Novel Protection Method for Hybrid Cascaded UHVDC Line Based on Control Response Characteristics
abstract: To address the issue of long-time protection gap between the traveling wave protection and pilot differential protection actions for high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission lines, a novel protection method for hybrid cascaded ultra high voltage direct current (HCUHVDC) line based on control response characteristics is proposed. The variations in the rectifier converter valve trigger angle and the inverter DC current command value are analyzed for faults at different locations. The command value change of DC current is characterized by the time difference between the start of the trigger angle increase and the start of the command value decrease. Characteristic curves of the increment of the trigger angle and the time difference are constructed for forward out-of-zone faults with different fault severity levels on the DC line. The point composed of the trigger angle increment and the time difference for the DC line fault is in the upper right corner of the point for the forward external fault. Based on this feature, a fault identification criterion is constructed. Finally, a ${\pm }$800kV hybrid cascaded model is built in PSCAD to verify the protection performance. Results show that the proposed scheme can accurately identify DC transmission line faults, with strong robustness against transition resistance and noise interference, thus possessing promising engineering application prospects.

title: Resonance Mitigation Effectiveness Evaluation and Damping Parameters Design Method for Parallel Resonance in Power System
abstract: Traditional methods evaluate and design resonance mitigation strategies by repeatedly solving system impedance, which results in low efficiency, limited scalability. There is a lack of universal and effective evaluation approaches to analyze the effectiveness of strategies for local/non-local resonances of multiple nodes and harmonic current amplifications in multiple resonance-participating branches. To address this issue, a parallel resonance mitigation domain (PRMD)-based effectiveness evaluation method for resonance mitigation strategies is proposed. By decoupling the strategies' equivalent impedance from the nodal impedance matrix, the method avoids repeated system matrix inversion, simplifying the evaluation process significantly. The relative mitigation domain (RMD) and ideal mitigation domain (IMD) for each domain of PRMD are further defined to guide optimal parameter selection. Based on this, a damping parameters design method based on IMD-PRMD is proposed to streamline the decision-making process and achieve comprehensive parallel resonance mitigation. The proposed method can be extended to any resonance scenario.

title: Commutation Failure Prediction for LCC-HVDC Based on CNN-LSTM-Attention Neural Network
abstract: Commutation failure (CF) can cause DC current surges, impaired system transmission power and even leading to HVDC blocking. The prediction of CF combined with early control triggering is beneficial for avoiding CFs. However, current analyses of CF identification mainly focus on real-time detection or prediction based on limited factors, which are insufficient for reliable CF prediction. Therefore, a CF prediction method for the line-commutated converter high-voltage direct current (LCC HVDC) system based on CNN-LSTM-Attention is proposed. Firstly, key indicators that represent the commutation state are selected by analyzing the factors that influencing CF. Secondly, a CF prediction model is constructed based on CNN-LSTM Attention. Additionally, the input data sampling principle is clarified and the commutation state discrimination component based on DC current variation is built for the model training. On this basis, a method for predicting CF is proposed. Finally, the accuracy and efficiency of the proposed method is validated based on the CIGRE LCC-HVDC Benchmark system and the Bin-Jin HVDC system in China.

title: Joint Type Diagnosis and Severity Assessment of Partial Discharge in Gas-Insulated Switchgear via Multi-Task Learning
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) is a key indicator of insulation health in gas-insulated switchgear (GIS). It is widely used for condition monitoring in high-voltage power systems. However, the diverse intensities and underlying fault mechanisms of PD often result in complex and variable signal patterns. Traditional single-task learning approaches struggle to capture this complexity and generalize across multiple diagnostic objectives. To address these challenges, we propose PD-MTNet, a multi-task learning framework for simultaneous PD type diagnosis and severity assessment. The framework adopts an attention-enhanced lightweight backbone to extract robust shared representations, tailored to the multi-scale and sparse nature of PRPD data. By highlighting salient discharge regions and suppressing background responses, the backbone effectively captures physically meaningful features across phase-amplitude scales. A multi-path hybrid module is then employed to decouple task-specific features according to their diagnostic mechanisms, facilitating more discriminative representations for each task. This design, together with the shared feature learning strategy, enhances intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. This design improves robustness to ambiguous boundaries and noisy labels, resulting in more stable and physically consistent diagnostic performance. Experimental results demonstrate that PD-MTNet achieves classification accuracies of 97.92% for PD type diagnosis and 95.19% for severity assessment, validating its effectiveness and generalization capability in complex PD diagnostic scenarios.

title: An Optimization-Guided Prediction-Free Two-Stage Real-Time Energy Management Strategy for Novel Co-Phase Traction Power Supply System With PV and Energy Storage
abstract: To overcome the challenge of large compensation capacity requirements in distributed continuous co-phase traction power supply system (TPSS), a novel co-phase TPSS (NCTPSS) is proposed. This system simultaneously tackles the problems of three-phase voltage unbalance and neutral sections commonly found in conventional electrified railways, while also providing interfaces for the integration of distributed renewable energy sources. When NCTPSS is integrated with photovoltaics (PV) and energy storage (ES), it enables the effective utilization of both regenerative braking energy (RBE) and renewable energy. However, due to the uncertainties associated with traction load (TL) and photovoltaics (PV), conventional prediction-optimization-based frameworks for real-time energy management strategy (EMS) face challenges such as high computational complexity and modeling difficulties. To address these issues, this paper proposes an optimization-guided prediction-free two-stage real-time EMS, consisting of an offline stage and a real-time stage. In the offline stage, an optimized dispatch library is generated based on historical TL and PV data to provide reference guidance and avoid myopic decision-making. In the real-time stage, a coordinated control strategy that combined optimization-guided EMS and rule-based EMS is proposed to ensure effective dispatch under various load scenarios. Finally, simulations and hardware-in-the-loop experiments are conducted to validate the performance of the proposed NCTPSS and EMS.

title: A Differential Decaying DC Component Based Unit Protection For Transmission Networks With SFCL
abstract: Several elements supervise transmission line protective relays to assure their security and selectivity. These elements are crucial for fault detection and interruption by various protection schemes. Superconducting fault current limiters (SFCLs) can inherently affect the currents and voltages, thereby impacting the performance of these protection elements. The influence of various SFCLs on transmission line unit protection strategies is investigated, and a differential decaying DC component (DDCCdiff) based logic is proposed in this paper. The DC component at each end is extracted using the adaptive modified FIR notch filter and the modified discrete Fourier transform technique. The energy of the DDCCdiff is estimated using the Hilbert transform, which is used as a fault detection index. Different test systems fitted with various SFCLs, modeled using EMTDC/PSCAD, are used for validation. The obtained findings, as assessed by simulating many disturbances, show that the proposed strategy is effective.

title: Discharge-Induced Surface Electrode Degradation in Metallized Film Capacitors: A Comparison under AC and DC Conditions for UHVDC Applications
abstract: Metallized film capacitors (MFCs) are widely used for DC voltage stabilization and AC harmonic filtering in converter stations of UHVDC systems. However, the growing demand for higher voltage and miniaturization poses challenges to the operating reliability of MFCs. This study employs adaptive signal decomposition denoising and image processing techniques to compare discharge signals and surface electrode degradation of metallized films under DC and AC conditions. A capacitance-reducing discharge (CRD) concept applicable to various operating conditions in converter stations is proposed, encompassing self-healing (SH), flashover around SH points, and margin flashover. Under DC conditions, CRD features high-intensity and more pronounced oscillations. Larger SH points account for 71.2% of capacitance reduction with distinct penetrating flashover paths being observed. Under AC conditions, SH points are smaller and more circular. Frequent flashover discharges cause extensive surface electrode evaporation, with flashover around SH points contributing 40.1% of the overall degradation. The energy of CRD exhibits a power-law relation with the applied voltage, with its exponent factor under DC stress twice that under AC stress. The findings provide theoretical support for the reliability of high-performance MFCs in UHVDC applications.

title: A Novel Independent PST Topology and Its Power Flow Regulation Characteristics
abstract: As the grid topologies and operating conditions become increasingly complex, the natural power flow distribution may become inefficient and uneven. Current power grids require effective power flow regulation devices. Phase shifting transformer (PST), leveraging its advantages of high regulation capacity and cost-effectiveness, has been widely adopted globally. However, traditional PST lacks a practical structural solution for decoupled amplitude-phase regulation. While independent PST (IPST) offers both a simple structure and two-dimensional regulation capability, they suffer from drawbacks like an abnormal regulation range and narrow adjustment zone. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel independent phase shifting transformer. First, based on its topology, we analyze the input-output characteristics. Quantitative characterization of the device's compensation range boundary is achieved by examining two constraint effects: those from the source side winding and load side winding. By integrating the bridge circuit commutation effect, we further expand the regulation area and double the number of adjustable points. Next, we derive the power flow regulation range expression using linear and translational transformations of the voltage characteristic equation. The dynamic variation patterns and extreme value formulas of the regulation range are then investigated. Finally, virtual simulations and physical experimental works verify that this topology enables decoupled regulation with a simple structure. The amplitude regulation range is 0.66-1.515, and the phase shifting range is -60° to 60°, with an error between experimental and theoretical values below 5%. Compared to traditional independent PST, it effectively optimizes the regulation range and increases the number of regulation points.

title: Real-Time Energy Management for Urban Rail Transit With Reversible Substations Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Efficiently utilizing the energy-saving potential of reversible converter (RC) has received significant attention in urban rail transit with reversible substations. However, energy management is considerably challenged by the highly dynamic and stochastic nature of train operations when relying on traditional methods. Therefore, a real-time energy management model based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is proposed in this paper. The model aims to minimize energy consumption through real-time decision-making, in which an agent dynamically optimizes RC control parameters using continuous state feedback from trains, traction substations (TSs), and main substations (MSs). A novel reward function is designed to incorporate both safety constraints and a day-ahead optimization benchmark, thereby effectively coordinating operational safety with energy efficiency. Moreover, stochastic timetable disturbances are introduced during training to enhance the model’s robustness. Simulations based on Qingdao Metro Line 3 demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly improves regenerative braking energy (RBE) utilization and reduces reverse power at the MSs, achieving a daily energy saving of 8.30%. Sensitivity analysis further quantifies the impact of key parameters, including RC capacity, step-down loads, and system scale, on overall performance. Finally, hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) experiments confirm the model’s practical effectiveness and robustness against communication delays, demonstrating its strong potential for real-world applications.

title: Robust Loop-Shaping Control for Medium-High Frequency Oscillations Mitigation in Grid-Connected Converters With Effective Hardware Implementation
abstract: This paper presents a robust control design framework for a three-phase grid-connected inverter using $H_{\infty }$ loop-shaping control to enhance renewable energy integration. To ensure hardware implementation in practice, the framework provides sufficient robustness against model uncertainties, minimizes the medium-high frequency oscillations caused by dead-time and switching interactions with the LCL filter, and prevents high-magnitude oscillations in the modulating signal to avoid saturation and performance degradation. For this purpose, loop-shaping weighting functions and D-stability techniques are employed, and the problem is formulated using linear matrix inequalities. Moreover, the proposed method integrates a Kalman filter to balance oscillation levels in the control input and to prevent modulating signal saturation. The filter dynamics are integrated into the design model to ensure the stability of the entire control structure. Simulation and experimental results, including the real-time simulation done using an OPAL-RT platform, confirm the superior performance, robustness, and practical feasibility of the developed control strategy in achieving accurate active and reactive power reference tracking while lowering the total harmonic distortion, even with weak grids and during generation-side disturbances. In contrast, other methods may encounter significant issues in the experimental setting, making their practical implementation challenging.

title: Prediction of Aeolian Vibrations in Conductors Equipped With Bretelles
abstract: Bretelles (damper-loops) are made of slack conductor pieces that are used to mitigate aeolian vibration amplitudes. Under cyclic and dynamic excitation, significant flexural hysteresis is induced by inter-strand friction within the wires of the bretelle, resulting in the dissipation of substantial amounts of energy. This study proposes a comprehensive method for modeling and predicting aeolian vibrations in transmission line conductors equipped with bretelles. This method employs a direct transient approach to predict the energy dissipation of bretelles and it uses a nonlinear numerical model that was developed for slack cable based on experimental bending tests. By incorporating empirical equations for wind power input and conductor self-damping power dissipation, and utilizing the Energy Balance Principle, vibration amplitudes expected on conductors are predicted. The predicted vibrational response and maximum amplitudes compared well with the laboratory and experimental line data available in the literature. The developed method allows for optimizing the geometrical and mechanical properties of bretelles when coupled with conductors, eliminating the need for additional experimental tests.

title: Thermal Analysis of EHV XLPE Cable Systems Using FEM During Pre-Qualification Assessment
abstract: The pre-qualification (PQ) assessment of Extra High Voltage (EHV) Cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) cable systems requires a year-long voltage application with 180 heating cycles as per IEC 62067. A key challenge in this assessment is maintaining the conductor temperature at 90-95$^{\circ }$C for the final two hours of every heating cycle, irrespective of installation and ambient conditions. As the test cable is energised, the conductor temperature is monitored in a parallel reference cable. Matching the sheath temperature in both reference and assessment cables ensures equivalent conductor temperature. The use of the physical reference cable increases the cost, test complexity, and instrumentation requirements due to prolong evaluation period. This paper proposes a MMA (Method of Moving Asymptotes) optimisation-based Finite Element Method (FEM) simulation approach to design a virtual reference EHV cable that replaces the physical reference cable. The virtual cable is used to find the ampacity range of EHV cables for different installations. In addition, a common current range that satisfies the IEC 62067 thermal limit across the installations is determined. The proposed method is validated against EHV PQ experimental data with three installations (under soil, cable-duct, and under the soil with High Density Polyethylene (HDPE) pipe). The study also identifies under soil HDPE as a critical installation requiring crucial temperature monitoring.

title: Numerical Simulation of Ion Flow Field and Multi-Factor Influence of Rotating Wind Turbine Tip Corona Discharge Under Thundercloud Electric Field
abstract: Rotating wind turbines are more vulnerable to lightning strikes than static wind turbine, possibly due to the different distribution of tip corona charges. However, there is a lack of research on the characteristics of blade tip corona charge distribution. This paper establishes a simulation model of corona charge distribution of rotating wind turbine. The long gap discharge test of the scaled wind turbine is carried out to verify the effectiveness of the simulation model. The simulation results show that the corona current increases with the increase of wind turbine speed, which is consistent with the test results. When the wind turbine rotates, the corona charge will migrate to the arc trajectory through which the blade rotates, which greatly reduces the charge density accumulated at the blade tip. Compared with the static state, the electric field intensity of the blade tip is higher when the wind turbine rotates, which will make it easier for the blade tip to initiate the upward leader. Moreover, the influence of different factors on the corona charge distribution of rotating wind turbine is calculated, and the function relationship between the maximum electric field intensity of the wind turbine tip and the rotation speed is established.

title: A Full-cycle Model of the AC Electric Arc Furnace Considering the Production Process
abstract: The existing electric arc furnace models mainly focus on the power quality issues generated during the melting period, failing to fully consider that the smelting process is a continuous and dynamic one. This results in the lack of a complete full-cycle model of the electric arc furnace, thereby restricting the assessment of power quality throughout the entire smelting process. Therefore, this paper proposes a full-cycle model of the AC electric arc furnace considering the production process. Firstly, by analyzing the influence of the production process on the furnace gas during the steelmaking process of the electric arc furnace, the dynamic mapping relationship between the gas concentration changing with time and the microscopic particle behavior in the arc was revealed using the electronic continuity equation. Secondly, based on the magnetic compression force balance equation, the quantitative relationship between pressure and radius was derived, and the function of the arc length change throughout the cycle was constructed. Thirdly, through a combination of mechanism and data, the gas concentration change curves and the arc length change functions for each stage of the smelting process were determined. Finally, using a 55-ton steelmaking AC electric arc furnace as the research object, a model was established on the Matlab/Simulink platform to verify its accuracy. The simulation results show that the proposed model is consistent with the actual production process of the AC electric arc furnace and can accurately reflect the entire power quality cycle of the entire period.

title: Thermomechanical modelling of clamping forces in power transformers with field data validation
abstract: Maintaining the mechanical integrity of a power transformer during large fault currents requires a clamping system that exerts sufficient compressive forces on the windings. This paper presents a thermomechanical model for the clamping force in a power transformer. The model predicts changes in clamping forces due to operating conditions, such as load and ambient temperatures, to indicate when the transformer is most vulnerable to mechanical failures. The model was tested and evaluated on one year of operational data collected from a 40 MVA ONAN transformer equipped with extensive temperature monitoring and novel clamping force sensors. By using only transformer design data, fundamental material parameters and results from the heat run test, the model was able to replicate the general trends observed in the measured clamping force. The model was able to predict the daily mean clamping force throughout the year with a mean absolute error of 6.6 kN, which corresponds to 2.9 % of the initial clamping force at the start of the year. For daily variations, i.e., the difference between maximum and minimum clamping force for each day, the model was able to predict variations with a mean error of 2.1 kN. However, the model overestimates the changes in clamping force, as it is too sensitive to changes in loading and ambient temperature.

title: Decoupled Detailed Equivalent Model for Parallel and Multi-Rate EMT-Type Simulation of Modular Multilevel Converter With Battery Energy Storage
abstract: Modular multilevel converters (MMCs) integrated with battery energy storage systems (BESS) enable efficient utilization of renewable energy resources such as wind and photovoltaic, while enhancing reliability and scalability of high-voltage direct current systems. This paper proposes a decoupled detailed equivalent model (D-DEM) for BESS-integrated MMC for electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation. The proposed model can accurately represent the dynamics of the converter under deblocking and blocking modes. To efficiently utilize available hardware resources, a multi-rate simulation technique is adopted to simulate the MMC subsystems with different time steps. Additionally, switching interpolation technique is proposed to accurately compensate for the intra-time-step switching events of the MMC multi-valves. To further accelerate the EMT simulation of MMC, a hybrid parallel computing EMT solver is implemented, using both central and graphical processing units (CPU-GPU). The accuracy of the proposed D-DEM is validated against a detailed model (DM) using Simulink/Simscape Electrical toolbox with 1 µs time step. The simulation efficiency of the proposed D-DEM is faster than the conventional DEM model by a factor of 2.81 with CPU-only implementation for the MMC with 400 submodules per arm. Furthermore, the proposed hybrid CPU-GPU solver achieves 79-fold faster than the CPU-only sequential implementation.
